What is being calculated?

A symmetric 2D model of feet, shanks, thighs, a rigid upper body and a point barbell load. Knee and shin trajectories are prescribed; trunk angle is solved for balance. Inertial terms are included when selected. The graph and moments use the same model as the moving figure.

Inverse dynamics computes joint moments from prescribed movement and external forces. OpenSim: Inverse Dynamics.

Model assumptions

Rounded segment masses, rigid segments and equal loading of both legs are assumed. The torso, head and arms form one segment. No individual muscle forces, joint contact forces, friction test or 3D motion is calculated. This is a new educational model, not a clinically validated or OpenSim-validated prediction.

Assumed ground support: −9 to +20 cm from the ankle. The centre-of-pressure marker can leave it; the simulation then flags infeasibility.
